text:
The Burned Warehouse
On Stewardship by Precedence in Kansas City
A didactic oration, in eight walks

I. The Fire

In the winter of 48 BC, Julius Caesar found himself besieged in Alexandria and was forced to a commander's decision. To deny his ships to the invading Egyptian fleet, he ordered them set ablaze in the harbor. It proved a successful tactic and the wooden fleet never sailed.

Fire, however, obliges no treaties. A blaze thus spread from the water into the city, and made feast of the warehouses at the docks, where a trove of scrolls was being stored: history, science, literature, all manner of human work. In but one night, say Plutarch, Dio, and Seneca, 40,000 scrolls burned to ash. Caesar saved his position but the great city was thus left with thousands of lost works: a moment forever inalterable, a humanity wrought unsaved.

Ponder for a moment what effectively a scroll is. It is a physical object but also an intellectual concept bound in one: the way a human is a body and yet furthermore an identity there beyond. The former gives rise to the latter. And consider what made the loss absolute. In the ancient world there was no second set shelved elsewhere, no copy in the cloud; each scroll was singular, and when it burned, the histories, and memories, and tragedies converted to smoke and ash na'er to be again. Burn the warehouse and you wound the living while silencing the dead forever.

Hold that background. And to that let us paint a new city on this canvas. Kansas City! Governed in a similar reckless, heedless, bull-headed self-defeating modus. it's small fires, set in the harbor legally and with good intentions, by men in awe each time at how the flames spread through the streets.

From the harbor, then, to the question the harbor forces.

II. The Steward's Question

The standard comes before the facts, for facts without a standard are only gossip.

A mayor is not a sovereign. A sovereign may raise monuments to his own glory and call it statecraft. A mayor, you see, is a steward, and the steward's question is single and cannot be evaded: does the household flourish under his hand? Not whether the favored rooms gleam. Whether the house still stands.

The Greeks had a name for the steward's art. Oikonomia: the ordering of the household, the wise keeping of what is entrusted. Our word economy descends from it, and the descendant has forgotten its father. We use it now to mean money changing hands, and we have mislaid the older and harder meaning: the care of the house itself, the roof, the stores, the souls within. The steward will be judged by the Greek meaning, whatever the modern one permits.

Walk with me through the exchange. A citizen asks the steward: What is the city?
The steward answers: The people.
Then the citizen asks: Why do the people wait, while the palace rises?
There is no reply, the question just drifts into silence. There is: record. Only the record will be read aloud. Yet, who authors the record?

Physicians have a word for what we are about to examine. Iatrogenics: when the healer does harm, when care and therapeutics become disease and downfall. It does not require malice. That is the entire terror of it. No cruelty need be intended for cruelty's work to be done; the road to iatrogenic ruin is paved with interventions nobody meant to be cruel. This is a key component as we continue, its recurrence may happen to be one of new dress: a monkey suit cutting ribbons. But it is nonetheless a presence oft encountered.

So the standard is set. Let us walk the city and read its ledger.

III. The Palace Over the Ashes

After the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, Nero built the Domus Aurea, the Golden House: a palace so vast it swallowed whole neighborhoods, with a revolving dining room and a bronze colossus of himself a hundred and twenty feet tall. The Romans believed it living satire, the way subject peoples do. Roma domus fiet, they said. Rome is becoming one house.

The palace is rubble now, built over and buried, its gold leaf long since picked from the walls. Yet the comedy prevails through the ages. As it goes with the erection of monuments: the stone is worn, tempus fugit, but the hope lives in lessons that are ingrained in minds. And a wise steward would be prescient as to which of the two his legacy is begetting. Stone or obstruction?

Look at Kansas City and tell me what it is becoming.

Let us read now its ledger aloud and without adornment: a $600 million city bond guarantee for a downtown Royals ballpark, serviced by projected revenues nobody has defined. Fifty-one million for the Luminary Park tunnel: that is fifty-one million to roof a downtown highway for a park, while the councilmen of the Fifth District, where the pools stand closed, ask: when will it be our turn? Forty-two and a half million in taxpayer money for World Cup renovations to Arrowhead, a holdover stadium the Chiefs will vacate for Kansas after 2030, while Missouri stares slack-jawed at a $150 million demolition bill for the husk this leaves behind. One hundred eighty-five million in public money for riverfront soccer.

And then the East Side's entry, written smaller, as such entries always are. The Sun Fresh grocery at 31st and Prospect: two owners in eight years, nineteen to twenty-nine million in public money depending on which outlet counted the ashes, and in the end: bare shelves, a blacked-out sign, and doors shut in August of 2025. this one grocery store could not be kept alive where people actually live. Nine figures could be found where they play, or perchance never see.

A generation after Nero, Juvenal looked at the whole arrangement and compressed it into three words that have outlived every palace ever built: panem et circenses. Bread and circuses. The emperors, and likewise our modern leaders, discovered that spectacle is so often cheaper than stewardship, and we the people were taught to accept the trade. It is worth saying plainly, since plainness is owed here: stadiums pacify. Deficits do not entertain.

But palaces are only half the account. Turn now from what was built to what was burned and consider the abjectness of loss.

IV. The Uncounted Scrolls

We observe flames growing, and it buries us downwind in the smoke of the burning scrolls.

Rome ran on the census. The empire counted its citizens, its grain, its legions; the acta diurna nailed the day's business to a board in the Forum, because even emperors understood that what is not recorded cannot be governed. A city, such as our own, which cannot quantify its failures and losses has sunk below the administrative standard of even antiquity, and all the more shameful in its free volition towards such. The ancients lost their records to fire. We are losing ours to indifference, which is fire without the excuse of accident.

In 2022, the Kansas City Police Department logged 7,587 violent-crime reports. Eighteen percent were cleared and sent to the prosecutor. Of the 24,356 property crime reports a mere 6.4 percent were cleared. Follow the shape of that failure carefully, because the curvatures are the fiasco: the pipeline does not die at the prosecutor's desk. It dies at investigation, before charging discretion ever enters the room. Jean Peters Baker, thirteen years the prosecutor, said it in words no spin can digest: "The problem is that I don't get them." What the police do not solve cannot be sent to her.

And when an arrest is made, ask where the arrestee sleeps. Kansas City closed its jail in 2009 and has rented beds ever since: 105 of them, split between Vernon and Johnson County, the men shipped to Nevada, Missouri and the women to Warrensburg. For lack of space, the booked are released after booking. The city's own officials concede this fed more vandalism, more theft. The voters were promised a $200 million city jail on a sales-tax renewal. The promise, like so many, exists as a rendering.

Now, in fairness, and fairness is owed even to men we indict: the police answer to a state-appointed board, where the mayor holds one vote of five. The clearance crisis belongs to investigators he does not command. But a steward who cannot command the watch may still cry alarm. He may still spend his coin where logical preservation dictates. Follow the coin, and see where it went. It went to the palace, not to the preservation of the city.

And here the scrolls imply a second truth, a darker, more human one. A burned scroll is data lost and denied all coming generations. Thus the city has not only failed to solve its crimes; it has let rot its capacity to count them, to account for its spending, to measure what its interventions cost. Posterity cannot audit what was never written down. So the tide of consequence stretches forward into all futurity, and it compounds in the dark, where no ledger is kept.

The scrolls counted, count now the streets.

V. The Ungoverned City

While the monuments rose, the machinery seized. Walk the columns.

Homelessness is up 170 percent in seven years: more than two thousand souls on any given night, by the city's own count. Of the chronically homeless, 95.7 percent sleep unsheltered, the highest percentage of any major city in the United States, per HUD. The city's own homelessness coordinator describes 214 providers running 333 programs and calls the system "incredibly siloed," money aligned around programs instead of outcomes. A councilwoman admits, on the record, that the city never really had a plan.

Set beside this the older standard. Rome fed its poor. The annona, the grain dole, was among the first duties the emperors dared not neglect; cynical as its motives were, the ships came in and the bread went out, because even a government of spectacle understood that the people must eat. Kansas City cannot keep one grocery open on its East Side. The emperors fed the mob to keep them quiet. We cannot stock a shelf. There is a kind of failure that shames even the cynics, and this is it.

Rents rose 4.7 percent year over year this spring, the fastest climb among America's fifty largest metros, while the national median fell. The bus system faces a $30 million shortfall with thirteen routes on the chopping block, the routes that carry the city's working poor. And the Jackson County assessment fiasco ended in a $250 million court-supervised settlement, the largest in county history: a remedy purchased at enormous cost, after the damage was done, because no one minding the store noticed the store was on fire.

And the settlements deserve their own column in this ledger, for they are its shadow. In five years alone the city has paid tens of millions in settlements, judgments, and claims, per the local accounting that titled its report fifty million and counting. The police department, which answers to the state and not to City Hall, paid nearly eleven million in a single budget year to settle misconduct and wrongful-death claims, against an allotment of two and a half. The council keeps signing: nine hundred thousand in one 2026 session, half of it to a former civil-rights director who said she was forced out. Whatever her personal cause may have been, it cost the citizens. A decade earlier it was two million for the discrimination suits out of the prosecutors' office, and a councilman said then what might be said now, that the city could do a better job on the front end. The front end never arrives. The city pays for the wrong and preserves the machinery that produced it; the settlement has become the budget line where accountability goes to be buried, and the citizenry pays the premium on a policy that never changes.

Set the two columns side by side and read them as one account. Billion-dollar downtown commitments sailed through council on schedule. The city's most basic human-need metrics sank to worst-in-the-nation. That is not a policy disagreement. A policy disagreement is arguable. This is a revealed preference, and preferences are destiny.

And a steward who will not be questioned will, in time, stop deserving answers.

VI. The Silenced

Mark the progression, for it is always the same. First the steward misspends. Then the city decays. Then the questions begin. Then the questions are managed.

The city criminalized knowingly being present as a spectator within two hundred feet of an unsanctioned automotive street event, with tow and impoundment for the watchers' cars. Two hundred feet. Standing near. A California court struck down a near-identical provision on First Amendment grounds. No court has tested Kansas City's version. It waits on the books, broad and loaded, like a question the city hopes nobody asks.

A Missouri attorney has formally accused the mayor of retaliating against a source, and of striking at his First Amendment rights, in a matter of nonprofit-funded Super Bowl travel with gift-rule questions trailing behind it. Mark it allegation, not finding; the distinction matters, and it will be considered here. Even so, it is the first such claim laid at the man's own door, and a record that omitted it would be a dishonest record.

And then the small exhibit, offered firsthand, for the orator may testify to what his own eyes have seen. I have writ on public forum my own conjecture and found that too subject to silencing. The ordinary coin of an ordinary man's private inclinations: that small change due each free citizen. More than once I found my commentary deleted amidst undisturbed speech, and it was a feckless display of a culture without scruples.

That is not moderation. That is curation.

The emperors had a practice for this, and a name for the practice: damnatio memoriae, the condemnation of memory. A name chiseled from the arch, a face cut from the stone, the man struck from the record as though he had never stood there. The steward commands a swifter instrument. No chisel is lifted; a keystroke suffices. But mark what the arch and the page have in common. A public official's page, maintained with public resources and used for public business, is not his parlor. When the steward begins editing the scrolls, the warehouse fire has reached the catalog itself.

Yet a charge that hides its counterweights is a smear. So the counterweights will now be weighed in the open.

VII. The Defense, Heard in Full

Let the defense speak, and let it speak completely.

Kansas City has a weak-mayor system; the mayor presides and persuades more than he commands. The police department answers to the state, not to City Hall. The new KCI terminal opened on his watch, on time, and the travelers noticed. Homicides have declined from their peak. He was reelected with 80.6 percent of the vote.

Every word of it is true. And none of it touches the thesis, because the thesis was never omnipotence. Unfitness for duty is not proved by control of everything. It is proved by priorities, and priorities are visible in any ledger. Rome invented the tribune because it distrusted unchecked power; but limited power was never a license for misdirected power, and the steward with one vote of five still chooses where his own coin goes. The mayor chose his fights: the stadiums, the World Cup, the war with Jefferson City. Those were choices. The record shows what they cost. The record shows what was left to rot while they were fought.

And here is the generosity the argument can afford, the generosity that makes it unanswerable: perhaps he believed the ballparks were stewardship. Perhaps every ribbon-cutting felt like service rendered. The record does not require us to decide what lived in his heart. It requires only that we read it. Iatrogenics never needed malice. It needs only a healer who never looked at what the treatment cost.

So the account is read. Now follow it forward, past our lifetimes.

VIII. The Tide Into Futurity

Return to Alexandria, for the parable is not finished.

The tragedy was never the tactic. Tactics work; that is why commanders choose them, and Caesar's fire did exactly what he asked of it. The tragedy was the blindness and the false pretense surrounding the action: the certainty that the fire would stay in the harbor, the refusal to price what stood downwind. And then the cruelest arithmetic of all, the one the commander never does: the scrolls were not the present's property alone. They were posterity's. Every generation after 48 BC inherited a smaller Alexandria, and not one of them was consulted.

So with Kansas City, scroll by scroll. Each necessary decision adds weight the next generation inherits without a vote: the debt service on the ballpark bonds, the unsolved cases aging into cold ones, the bus routes that never come back, the assessment bills that broke fixed incomes, the records never kept and therefore never reckoned with. The debts we wrote down; the deeds we did not. Posterity will pay the first and never know the second. The goal was helping. The helping became the harm. That is what iatrogenic means. It is the most expensive kind of failure, because it spends the moral credit of good intentions and leaves the city poorer in revenue and in trust alike.

The steward's question was single, and it cannot be evaded. Did the household flourish under his hand?

A city is not measured by what its stewards intend but by what they are willing to let burn, and Kansas City has been governed these seven years by a leadership that chose the palace over the warehouse, the spectacle over the scrolls, and the announcement over the account: unfit for duty not because it wished harm upon anyone, but because it never once looked at the price we have to pay.

text:
My response to Mao's the famine during the Great Leap Forward from reader _@wwwervelwind:

The Famine of the Great Leap Forward was caused by Mao's pride after the Soviet split. He wanted to pay off all loans from the USSR in 5 years instead of 16 years. All weapons and industrial equipment that USSR gave to China were loans and not gift. China had to pay compensation to USSR for terminating early the lease for South Manchurian Railway and Port Arthur (USSR's only warm water port in Dalian). As China had no hard currency like the USD to payoff the loan it had to export most of its agricultural and steel surplus to the USSR. 

Summary of the deadliest mechanics of the Great Chinese Famine (1959–1961). The catastrophe was not caused by a single mistake, but by a deadly feedback loop where political terror, inflated statistics, ideological pride, and forced debt repayments reinforced one another.

See table image attached below.

1. The Dynamic of "Faked Harvest Reports" (Wind of Exaggeration)
Under the political pressure of the Great Leap Forward, local provincial and commune cadres were terrified of being purged as "rightists" or anti-revolutionaries if they failed to meet impossible agricultural quotas.

The  Competition of Lies: Cadres engaged in frantic competition, reporting "bumper harvests" where wheat and rice yields were artificially  inflated by 200%, 300%, or even 500%.

The Requisition Trap: The central government calculated state grain procurements based on these fictional reports. When Beijing ordered      the state to take its standard percentage (e.g., 30%), it was taking 30%  of an imaginary giant number. In reality, that percentage amounted      to 80% to 100% of the actual physical grain harvested, leaving      peasants with nothing to survive on.

2. Mao's "Surplus" Illusion Meets National Pride
In 1958 and early 1959, because of these faked reports, Mao and the Politburo genuinely believed China had produced so much food that Mao famously pondered in public speeches: "What are we going to do with all this excess grain?"

When relations with the Soviet Union fractured in 1960, Mao's response was governed by fierce geopolitical pride:

Refusing to Show Vulnerability: Rather than admitting economic distress or requesting debt relief from Nikita Khrushchev, Mao declared at the   Beidaihe Conference (July 1960) that China would "tighten its  belt" (ya zhengqi) and pay off the entirety of its ~1.4  billion ruble debt to the USSR in 5 years instead of 16.

Rejecting  Soviet Offers: When the Soviets realized the severity of the famine in  1961 and offered a loan of 1 million tons of grain and 500,000 tons of  Cuban sugar, the Chinese leadership turned down the grain offer to      maintain ideological superiority, accepting only the sugar.

3. The Human Toll at the Village Level
To meet the accelerated debt timeline, specialized foreign trade teams were sent into the countryside to enforce grain collection:

State   agents confiscated seed grain (meant for the next planting season) and  feed grain, sealing local communal granaries under armed guard.

Millions  of tons of grain, soybeans, pork, and canned goods were trucked directly      to rail hubs and shipped across the Soviet border to clear the debt      ledger.

Peasants   were forbidden from leaving their villages to search for food under strict  household registration (hukou) controls, leading to mass starvation      across provinces like Anhui, Henan, Sichuan, and Gansu.

Summary
The famine was fundamentally a man-made distribution and political policy disaster. Falsified local reports led Beijing to overestimate China's food supply, and Mao’s determination to prove China's independence from Moscow led him to export actual food reserves during the peak of a domestic starvation crisis.

China succeeded in clearing its debt to the Soviet Union ahead of schedule by 1965, but at the cost of an estimated 30 to 45 million human lives.

So in Deng-era, alot of efforts were placed in auditing of information submitted by provincial cadres that they have met their KPIs. Remember they had no internet during Mao's era so everything had to be tabulated by hand and then sent via telegram to Beijing. Mao is the peasant emperor - he is not very sophisticated in the use of modern information technology and auditing techniques.

text:
Empty Seats in Mobile: What a Rally Reveals When the Faithful Stop Filling the Room

Jessiah, who hosts Pondering Politics, took Friday night in Mobile and refused to treat it as a lighting problem. President Trump spoke at the Mitchell Center at the University of South Alabama, a room that holds 10,041, and the photographs do not argue. Rows behind him were bare. The second deck thinned out in the corners. A president who has spent a decade measuring love by how full the hall looks stood in front of a hall that did not fill.

The card around him tells you why the night was built. Senator Tommy Tuberville, now running for governor, was on the stage. Representative Barry Moore is running for the Senate seat Tuberville is leaving. Jerry Carl and Rhett Marques were there for House races, Marques in a redrawn Second District the party drew to keep. This was not a nostalgia tour. It was a midterm errand, a month out, in a state that does not make a Republican sweat. If the room will not fill in Mobile, the errand is already in trouble.

The promises did not change to match the room. Trump again offered a check, on the order of $5,000 a citizen, if Republicans hold Congress. He shouted out Laura Loomer from the stage. Natalie Harp was with the traveling party. The White House had no comment on the empty seats. A crowd that leaves, or never arrives, is a fact. A slogan about sold-out love is a claim. The photographs are the grader.

Jessiah's point is the old one about authority. A movement that lives on presence cannot survive absence and call it a conspiracy. Loyalty that has to be narrated over empty chairs is already negotiating the exit. Byron Donalds taking a distance in Florida, candidates scrubbing a name off a website, a Deep South arena with daylight between the seats: these are not one bad advance team. They are a coalition pricing the cost of the man.

A seminary would call it a failure of witness. You cannot preach a kingdom you will not sit through. The midterms will count the chairs the rally would not.

text:
Law enforcement officers lose qualified immunity when a plaintiff proves both that the officer violated a “Constitutional Right” and that “The Right” was clearly established at the time of the incident.

How Qualified Immunity Fails in Court
Under the two-part test used by courts, an officer is denied protection if: 

•A constitutional violation occurred: 
The officer's conduct (such as using excessive force or conducting an unlawful search) violated the U.S. Constitution. 

•The law was clearly established: 
Existing precedent (from the U.S. Supreme Court, a federal appeals court, or a state supreme court) made it apparent and obvious to a reasonable officer that their specific conduct was unlawful. 

Scenarios Where Immunity Does Not Apply
Qualified immunity protects civil servants from personal monetary liability in civil lawsuits, but it does not apply in other contexts: 
•Criminal charges: 
Qualified immunity only shields officers from civil suits, meaning it offers no protection against criminal prosecution by state or federal authorities. 

•Municipal liability: 
The defense applies to individual officers, not to local government entities or cities themselves. 

•Injunctive relief: 
Plaintiffs seeking court orders to stop a specific police policy or practice rather than financial damages can bypass the doctrine

FYI : For anyone who doesn’t know what is meant by a “1983”
Section 1983 (codified at 42 U.S. Code § 1983) is a federal civil rights law that allows people to sue state and local government officials who violate their constitutional rights or federal laws while acting under government authority. 

Originally enacted as part of the Civil Rights Act of 1871 (also known as the Ku Klux Klan Act), the statute was designed during Reconstruction to protect newly freed individuals and combat lawlessness by public officials. 
Today, it serves as a primary legal tool to hold government actors accountable. 

How Section 1983 Works
•Does not create rights: 
Section 1983 does not grant new civil rights; instead, it provides a legal mechanism to enforce rights that already exist under the U.S. Constitution or federal statutes. 

•Under color of law: 
The defendant must have acted "under color of state law," meaning they used their official position, badge, or government authority to commit the wrongful act. 

•Proving a claim: 
A plaintiff must show that a state or local actor deprived them of a federal right and that this violation caused actual harm or injury. 

Common Examples of Claims
•Police misconduct: 
Cases involving excessive force, police brutality, wrongful arrest, or false imprisonment. 

•Jail and prison conditions: 
Situations where correctional staff show "deliberate indifference" to an inmate's serious medical needs or safety. 

•Constitutional violations: 
Infringements on free speech, religious freedom, or due process protections guaranteed by the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments. 

Available Remedies
•Damages: 
Financial compensation for medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering, or wrongful death.

•Injunctive relief: 
Court orders requiring a government agency or official to change a policy or stop specific misconduct.

•Attorney's fees: 
Compensation to help cover the legal costs of bringing the lawsuit

text:
How Did the “Guru Brahma” Shloka Originate?

“Guru Brahma, Guru Vishnu,
Guru Devo Maheshwaraḥ;
Guru Sakshat Parabrahma,
Tasmai Shri Gurave Namaha.”

This shloka is very familiar to all of us.
But what is the story behind it?
Who first uttered these words, and why?

There is a traditional story associated with this shloka, regarded as a beautiful expression of devotion and unwavering faith in one’s Guru.

Once, there lived a poor boy named Kautsa. A teacher named Vidyadhara took him into his ashram and taught him all the knowledge he possessed.

Once, the Guru had to leave the ashram for a few days. Until his Guru returned, Kautsa took great care of the ashram.

After some time, Kautsa completed his education. His parents came to take him home. But Kautsa firmly refused, saying:

“I will not leave my Guru.”

After his parents left, the Guru asked him why he was so determined to stay.

Kautsa replied:

“Gurudeva, when you were away, I examined your horoscope. It indicated that you might soon suffer from a serious illness. That is why I cannot leave you.”

Just as Kautsa had predicted, the Guru later contracted tuberculosis.

Since there was no proper treatment for the disease in those days, the Guru and his disciple went to Kashi, with the intention of performing sacred acts, charity and other meritorious deeds.

Seeing the Guru’s condition, many people in Kashi were repulsed by his illness. Some even advised Kautsa:

“Leave such a diseased Guru and go your way.”

But Kautsa refused to abandon his Guru.

According to the story, the Trimurtis—Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshwara—decided to test Kautsa’s unwavering devotion to his Guru.

First, Lord Brahma, disguised as an ordinary person, came and advised Kautsa to leave his Guru. Kautsa did not listen.

Then Lord Vishnu, also in disguise, came and gave him the same advice. Kautsa still refused to change his decision.

Finally, Lord Shiva himself came and advised him to leave his Guru.

But Kautsa firmly replied:

“Whoever may tell me to do so, I will never abandon my Guru.”

Pleased with his devotion, Lord Shiva asked him:

“What boon do you desire?”

Kautsa did not ask for anything for himself. Instead, he prayed:

“Please ensure that no one ever again advises me to abandon my Guru. Instead, protect my Guru.”

Moved by his selfless devotion, the Trimurtis appeared before him and offered to grant him liberation.

Then Kautsa humbly said:

“It was my Guru who introduced me to Brahma.
It was my Guru who introduced me to Vishnu.
It was my Guru who introduced me to Maheshwara.
And it is because of my Guru that I have reached a state where I can see You directly today.

Therefore, for me, my Guru is Brahma.
For me, my Guru is Vishnu.
For me, my Guru is Maheshwara.
For me, my Guru is verily Parabrahma.”

And thus, the story says, these words praising the greatness of the Guru came to be:

🌺 Guru Brahma, Guru Vishnu
🌺 Guru Devo Maheshwaraḥ
🌺 Guru Sakshat Parabrahma
🌺 Tasmai Shri Gurave Namaha

The story further says that Kautsa did not ask the Trimurtis to grant him liberation. Instead, he prayed that his Guru be granted liberation.

Moved by his unwavering devotion, the Trimurtis are said to have blessed his Guru with liberation.

True devotion to the Guru is not merely about seeing the Guru as God…

It is about walking the path shown by the Guru.

Śrī Gurubhyo Namaḥ 🌹🙏🌹

Pete Spinuzzi, Candidate for Walker River Justice of the Peace
Pizen Switch Times   October 17, 2024
Pizen Switch Times: Candidates for local offices are welcome to send their candidacy announcement  for publication in “Elections”.

“I am Pete Spinuzzi, candidate for Walker River Justice of the Peace.

The Walker River Justice Court is located in Yerington at the justice complex. Walker River Justice Court encompasses Silver Springs, Yerington, Mason Valley and Smith Valley.

Tanks, trucks, artillery, and pack animals stretched along the roads. From Italian Somaliland, another force prepared to advance from the east.

There had been no declaration of war. There did not need to be. Fascism did not regard treaties as obligations or weaker nations as equals. They were merely obstacles.

Benito Mussolini had promised Italians a new Roman Empire. He wanted colonies, military glory, and the restoration of national pride. Most of all, he wanted to erase the memory of Adwa. In 1896, an Ethiopian army had defeated an invading Italian force there, preserving Ethiopia’s independence. It was one of the most humiliating defeats ever inflicted upon a European colonial power in Africa.

Nearly forty years later, Fascist Italy came back with airplanes, tanks, machine guns, and poison.

Ethiopia was a member of the League of Nations. So was Italy. Both had pledged to respect the independence of other member states and submit disputes to peaceful settlement.

Mussolini knew this. He simply did not care.

His regime had spent years teaching Italians that war was not a tragedy but a purification. Fascism worshiped strength, obedience, national destiny, and the state. It presented mercy as weakness and conquest as evidence of vitality. Mussolini did not conceal his contempt for peace. He taught that permanent peace was neither possible nor desirable.

Now an African nation would pay the price for that creed.

The imbalance was staggering. Many Ethiopian soldiers marched in traditional clothing. Some carried modern rifles, but others possessed weapons dating from the nineteenth century. They faced an industrial army equipped with hundreds of aircraft and artillery pieces. Yet they fought hard.

Farmers, herdsmen, provincial levies, and imperial soldiers gathered beneath their commanders. They moved across mountains and ravines, often carrying their own food. They charged positions defended by machine guns. They died in numbers that will never be known with certainty.

Italian propaganda portrayed the invasion as a civilizing mission. Meanwhile, Italian aircraft began dropping mustard gas.

The poison fell in bombs and descended as an oily mist. It burned exposed skin, blinded its victims, and entered their lungs. Men who had survived the bombing collapsed later in agony. Watering places and retreat routes were contaminated. Medical workers struggled to treat injuries they had never seen and could not cure.

Italy had signed the Geneva Protocol prohibiting chemical warfare. Mussolini authorized its use anyway.

That was fascism in practice. Law applied only when it served the state. Treaties restrained only the weak. If an atrocity advanced the nation, the atrocity became virtue.

Even the Red Cross offered uncertain protection. Italian aircraft bombed hospitals and ambulances displaying its emblem. Historical estimates identify between seventeen and twenty-three attacks upon medical installations during the war. In December 1935, bombs struck hospitals at Dessie while Emperor Haile Selassie was directing the defense from the town. The message was unmistakable: there would be no sanctuary.

DigitalOcean Holdings introduced Agent Droplets on October 1, 2026, a monthly subscription that bundles Managed Agents capabilities into one bill, the company said in a Business Wire release from Broomfield, Colorado, and on its investor newsroom and blog.

Managed Agents entered public preview on September 22 with a managed runtime, governed access to more than 16,000 tools, Serverless Inference, and persistent agent memory and storage. Agent Droplets package those pieces as Pro at $50 a month with a 15 percent discount on included resources, and Team at $200 a month with a 20 percent discount. The bundle covers a harness runtime of dedicated microVM sandboxes that the company said start in about a second and resume from pause in about 300 milliseconds in DigitalOcean testing, plus an inference engine for DigitalOcean-hosted open models including Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3, and an Action Gateway for governed tool access with credentials kept outside the agent. Frontier models such as Claude and GPT remain pay-as-you-go at list price. Every size includes unlimited agents with no seat charges, observability, and enterprise security features named as single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, role-based access, audit logs, cloud firewalls, and DDoS protection. Customers choose whether spending stops at the plan price or continues at list prices after the allowance is used. DigitalOcean also announced Inference and Agents Balance, a prepaid balance from $5 to $500 usable only for Serverless Inference, Action Gateway, and Managed Agents. New customers can start with a $5 promotional credit and no card, subject to eligibility and the company's promotional terms. Agent Droplets and the prepaid balance are available today in regions where Managed Agents is offered. The release states Agent Droplets and Managed Agents are public preview services, and DigitalOcean does not guarantee production-level performance for preview services. Those start and resume timings are DigitalOcean's own test figures.

Why it matters: a dated, priced agent subscription with named model and tool bundles, and with public-preview status kept explicit rather than treated as general availability. Sources: DigitalOcean / Business Wire, 1 Oct 2026.

text:
Trump Signals New Action Against Iran, Sends About 9,000 More Troops to Middle East
Washington: US President Donald Trump has hinted at the possibility of fresh action against Iran, saying the US military is sending about 9,000 more troops to the Middle East aboard a group of naval vessels. According to the Associated Press, the group includes more than 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines.
The deployment includes the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group, which recently deployed alongside the cruiser USS Chosin, and the USS Iwo Jima-type amphibious force, the USS Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, which comprises the amphibious ships USS John P. Murtha and USS Anchorage. A US official, speaking to AP on condition of anonymity, said three American aircraft carrier groups could be in the region by the end of October. With the new deployment, the number of US sailors and Marines in the region will exceed 20,000, along with hundreds of aircraft.
The USS George H.W. Bush, USS George Washington and the USS Boxer Amphibious Ready Group are currently in the region. The George Washington normally operates in the Pacific but was sent to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose crew spent more than 260 consecutive days at sea during its extended deployment. The US Navy also deployed three carrier strike groups to the region in April, the first time that had happened since 2003.
In an interview with Time magazine published Thursday, Trump said it is possible to step up bombing in Iran after the November 3 US elections. Asked for more details, he said he could not share more about his strategy.
Ceasefire proposal rejected
Trump said he has rejected a ceasefire proposal from Iran, saying that what he would not accept a year ago, he would not accept today. He said Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy shipping route, but that the overall proposal was not good enough.

Back to the Sacred Geometry from a Catholic Christian perspective. I included an image of the Philosopher's Stone. I will supply @Grok output that I gleaned about viewing the Alchemical Philosopher's Stone from a Catholic Christian perspective as Jesus Christ dwelling in the soul.
This most perfectly happens in the Most Holy Eucharist, the Body Blood, Soul, and Divinity of Jesus, Substantially and Sacramentally, which we receive at Holy Mass.
The Grok output also explains the relations to this idea about the Philosopher's Stone and the Catholic Christian Kabalistic Tree of Life and the Catholic view as the Ever Blessed Virgin Mary as the Tree of Life as well.  
The Philosopher’s Stone is not first a laboratory object. In the Christian-alchemical tradition it is the Lapis Christi—the perfected, incorruptible substance that unites heaven and earth, spirit and matter, the divine and the human. That union is given its classic geometric formula in the Rosarium Philosophorum and later in Michael Maier’s Atalanta Fugiens: 
“Make of the man and the woman a circle, of that a square, of the square a triangle, of the triangle a circle, and you will have the Stone of the Philosophers.”
The figures are not arbitrary. They map the Great Work onto the mystery of the Incarnation.
The Triangle as the Most Holy Trinity An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles that nevertheless form one single surface. Medieval and Renaissance writers therefore used it as the simplest visual confession of the Athanasian Creed: three distinct Persons, one undivided Essence.
The three vertices stand for Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; the single enclosed space stands for the one Godhead. In some diagrams the triangle is even called “infinite,” because each angle is maximal and yet they coincide in one maximum—an image Nicholas of Cusa and earlier writers already applied to the Trinity.
The Circle as the Blessed Virgin Mary
The circle has no beginning and no end; it is the figure of eternity and of the perfect vessel. In the same tradition the circle is identified with Mary for two interlocking reasons:
She is the vas spirituale, the spiritual vessel that contained the Uncontainable. The infinite God who cannot be circumscribed chose to be circumscribed in her womb. Jean de Meung (and later Cusanus) therefore speak of “this triangular circle or circular triangle in the Virgin’s womb”—the Trinity itself made present inside a finite, created circle.
She is the immaculate matrix, the “philosophical Mercury” or white tincture from which the red Stone (Christ) is born. In the early-fifteenth-century Franciscan Buch der Heiligen Dreifaltigkeit Mary personifies the purified feminine principle; her Coronation by the Trinity is the visual climax of the white work that precedes the appearance of the red Stone.
Thus the circle is not merely “around” the triangle; it is the living enclosure in which the Trinity elects to act. The fiat of the Virgin is the moment the infinite triangle becomes a circle without ceasing to be a triangle.  How the two figures generate the Stone
Man and woman (sulfur and mercury, or Christ and Mary) first form a circle: the coniunctio, the sacred marriage inside the sealed vessel that is Mary’s womb.  That circle is squared: the four elements are separated and purified (the Passion of Our Lord Jesus Christ).
The square becomes a triangle: body, soul, and spirit—or the three Persons—are brought into explicit relation.
The triangle is returned to a circle: the Resurrection and the Assumption, the perfected Stone that is at once Christ and the deified creation that Mary already anticipates.
In short, the triangle-with-circle is the geometric confession that the Most Holy Trinity chose to accomplish the Great Work inside the Blessed Virgin. The Stone is the Child who issues from that circular womb, the same Child who is also the Cornerstone rejected by the builders. The geometry simply makes visible what the liturgy already sings: Ave, vas spirituale—Hail, vessel of the Spirit, in whom the Trinity itself became flesh.
There are two circles in the figure. They are not the same circle. The whole Work is the movement from the first to the second.
The outer circle is the One: eternity, the sealed vessel, the womb that can hold what cannot be held. In the language of this conversation it is Mary— the Catholic Christian Kabbalistic Binah and Malkuth at once, the Immaculate Heart as embassy, the boat of refuge, "Stella Maris", the Blessed Virign Mary as "Star of the Sea", marking a horizon that does not move. It is also the Father’s undivided essence crowning the Catholic Christian Kabbalistic Tree, Keter as a ring rather than a point. Nothing of the Work happens outside this circle. Saint Joseph’s Most Chaste Heart is the lock on its rim: the vessel stays closed.
Inside that circle the triangle is the Trinity—Father, Son, and Spirit, or body, soul, and spirit, or the three Sacred, Immaculate, and Chaste Hearts beating as one without confusion of Persons. This is the “marvelous triangle in the Virgin’s womb” and the three Persons who make their abode in the soul that keeps the commandments.
The square inscribed in the triangle is creation as Saint Francis sang it: Brother Sun, Sister Moon, Brother Fire, Sister Water, Sister Mother Earth. It is the four elements that must be separated and purified, the Passion of Our Lord Jesus Christ that ripens the Fruit on Saint Bonaventure’s Tree, the Catholic Christian Kabbalistic Gevurah’s shield and Chesed’s chalice. The human will is squared here—limited, named, offered.
The inner circle, the one resting inside the square, is the Philosopher’s Stone itself. It is Christ formed in the soul. It is the Catholic Christian Kabbalistic Tiferet: the Sacred Heart of Jesus on the Cross at the center of Maria, Arbor Vitae, "Mary, Tree of Life". It is the Fruit of the Tree of Life. It is the Kingdom within you. It is the child born when Mary has taken root. It is the soul that has been granted asylum in the Sacred and Immaculate Hearts and is no longer swimming in the sea but is itself a small, perfect heaven—the same shape as the outer circle, now generated inside the Work.
That is the axiom drawn as geometry:
> Make of man and woman a circle (the first belonging, the consecration, Joseph and Mary as one house),
> of that a square (the elements, the Cross, creation redeemed),
> of the square a triangle (the Most Holy Trinity dwelling),
> of the triangle a circle (the Stone—Jesus living in the place where Mary and Joseph already live).
The inner circle does not replace the outer. It repeats it at a higher octave. The soul does not become a fourth Person of the Trinity. It becomes the little circle that can exist only because the great circle—Mary, the vessel, the embassy of the two Hearts, guarded by the Chaste Heart—was never broken. The same God who is the circumference is now the center. The Gate of Heaven is the moment you notice that the two circles are one mystery: the Woman who contained the Uncontainable, and the soul in which that containment is allowed to happen again.
The outer circle is eternity. Creation is what it contains, not what it is.
A circle has no beginning and no end. That is why the Fathers and the medieval doctors used it for God: the One who is not measured by before and after. Nicholas of Cusa’s infinite circle, and the old Hermetic line that God is a sphere whose center is everywhere and circumference nowhere, say the same thing. Eternity is not a very long time. It is the undivided Now that holds every moment without being one of them.
In the squared circle that Now is the outer ring. Inside it the triangle is the Trinity, the square is creation, and the inner circle is the Stone.
The square is Francis’s four: Brother Sun, Sister Moon, Brother Fire, Sister Water, Sister Mother Earth. It has corners. It begins and ends. It can be wounded and redeemed. The outer circle does not. It embraces the square the way eternity embraces time—without being stretched by it, and without leaving any creature outside its care.
That is the difference between the two circles. The outer circle is uncreated. It is the Father’s essence, Keter as a ring rather than a point. The inner circle is created and then perfected: Christ formed in the soul, the Kingdom within, the Fruit. The outer circle does not become the inner one. It makes the inner one possible by never breaking.
Mary belongs to this figure as the created vessel that most perfectly receives the outer circle into time. She is not eternity. She is the womb in which the Eternal chose to be contained. Saint Bonaventure’s soil, Saint Louis Marie de Montfort’s roots, the boat of refuge, the Gate of Heaven—all of these are the outer circle touching the square at one point, Nazareth, and remaining the circumference of the whole Work. Saint Joseph’s Most Chaste Heart is the lock on that rim: creation is fenced so the Eternal can enter without the vessel leaking.
So the outer circle relates to creation by containing it, and to eternity by being it. Everything mentioned—the Tree, the three Hearts, the Canticle, the asylum, the Stone—happens inside that ring. Nothing of the Work is outside God. The square is the world. The triangle is the Three who dwell in it. The inner circle is the soul made a little heaven. The outer circle is the heaven that was never made, and that never ceases to hold them all.
The same geometry that the Christian alchemists used for the Stone is already the geometry of the interior life.
The triangle is the Most Holy Trinity. The circle is the vessel that can receive Them without being shattered. In the first Incarnation that vessel was the Immaculate Virgin. In the second, hidden incarnation that vessel is the consecrated soul in the state of grace.
Saint Louis de Montfort is explicit that Mary’s kingdom, like Christ’s, is not first a visible realm. “The kingdom of Jesus Christ consists principally in the heart, or interior, of man—according to the words, ‘the kingdom of God is within you’—so does the kingdom of Mary. The Blessed Virgin reigns principally in the interior of man, that is to say in his soul.”​, as stated by Catholic Way Publishing which I believe wholeheartedly elucidates this in their publishing of St Louis Marie de Montfort’s work.
Scripture already names the two movements that meet in that interior circle. 
Jesus says, “Abide in me, and I in you” (John 15:4). He also says, “If a man love me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him” (John 14:23). The Spirit is given as the one who “dwelleth with you, and shall be in you” (John 14:17). St Paul simply calls the baptized body “the temple of the Holy Ghost” (1 Cor 6:19).
Because of perichoresis—the mutual circumincession of the Three Persons—wherever one Person is substantially present, the other two are present with Him.
The Father is in the Son, the Son in the Father, the Spirit in both; therefore the soul that is the temple of the Spirit is the dwelling of the whole Trinity. The triangle does not arrive in pieces.
Mary’s presence in the soul does not compete with that indwelling; it is the created condition the Trinity Himself chose for It. De Montfort’s logic is the logic of the Annunciation repeated: the Holy Spirit finds His Spouse already living in a soul & therefore works there as He worked in Nazareth—forming Jesus. “The more clearly He sees Mary… living in a soul, the more mightily He works to bring forth Jesus in that soul, and that soul in Jesus.”​, as stated by the St de Montfort book adaptation by Eddie Doherty, which upon reflection shows exactly is meant by this.
The circle (Mary in the soul) is not an extra god. It is the womb in which the triangle begets the Son again.
That is why the old axiom—“make of man and woman a circle, then a square, then a triangle, then a circle”—can be read as the itinerary of consecration.
The soul & Mary form one circle of belonging. The four elements of the old man are purified. The three theological virtues (or the three Persons acting) stand forth as a triangle. The final circle is the soul become, by grace, what Mary already is by privilege: a living temple in which the Trinity makes Its home and the Kingdom is no longer only “among you” but within you.
The Stone, in this reading, is not a mineral. It is Christ formed in the soul that has become Mary’s dwelling, so that the Trinity that already circuminhabits Itself now circuminhabits the creature. “He who abides in Me, I will abide in him.” The circle does not replace the triangle. The circle is the place the triangle chose to rest.
The next post contains an image of you in a photo shoot from early on that I found that has you smirking and making a funny face with your finger as a mustache. I labeled it interactionism. The black and white image was striking and I found the playful nature of it to engender your fun attitude. You always seemed so perky and upbeat.
The post goes on the explain about the sociological perspective of symbolic interactionism and how we as humans ascribe meaning to things and act towards them on that basis.
The comment continues to state how words, going back to the previous reply about Alfred Korzybski as well as Marshall McLuhan, can occupy a semiotic space and can be symbols to our ideas about things not the things themselves.
The analogy I can draw is like that I've mentioned here and in previous replies about the Catholic Christian view of the Kabalistic Tree of Life and seeing it as symbol. Also the preciously stated Sacred Geometry seen though a Catholic Christian lens as well as the Catholic Christian point of view about the Philosopher’s Stone, Lapis Christi.
The counterpoint to this is Holy Mother Church's Sacraments which are actually the things they Sacramentally signify and are not mere symbols.
The post posits further symbolic interactionists are believers in a physical reality but by an individual's social definitions and that social definitions develop in in relation or in part to something real. They claim that people may not respond directly to this reality as such but to a social understanding of reality; responding indirectly through filters or like eyeglasses (perspectives).
I do not necessarily ascribe to these views as I have an understanding from a Thomistic perspective, that is of Saint Thomas Aquinas, believing in an actual reality we can sense which was created by God and was deemed by him as good.
As the next post shows, an image of @EllieGoulding from  a @Cosmopolitan December issue. I found this image to be evocative of the comment I posted with it about dancing with her hands up by her head like she was dancing. I fancied the wardrobe she was attired with with the blue background. She looked glamorous in photo albeit a little hazy.
I commented with the short Never Stop Dancing! I got this particular comment from a person @SeanBaby knows as Nico but I don't know if that is her name or Lindsay or what. She was a blogger I loved to read and really influenced my ideas about things for quite some time and some of whose book interests I took up as my own.
This was before my reversion to Catholicism and I do not find a lot of her ideas appealing anymore, though there is a lot of good left. I will not mention where she blogged or how I came to learn of her "on the Internet". I do however pray for her as she has a colossal mind and is a good person.
The particular quote I used was one she used more than once along with the phrase Ever Upward! I enjoyed both comments.
The first reminds me a proverb, which reminds me of the Perichoresis, a Greek term, which is the co-inherence and mutual indwelling of the Most Holy Trinity between the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit living completely through and in one another. 
The proverb goes "They who dance are thought mad by those who hear not the music". It is an old proverb misattributed to Fredrick Nietzsche. Nico/Lindsay quoted this proverb as well.
The second comment of Ever Upward! at the time I found to be esoteric of rising and spiraling upward to Heaven. I now take this as an expression of the Catholic Christian desire to become divinized in  Christ's Mystical Body through Baptism. This view of theosis/deification is the belief that out of sheer love, God invites humans to share in his divine life and nature.
This is done in Holy Mother Church through the Sacraments and Sacramental Grace. It is by Grace and not by personal substance or nature that this is accomplished.
It is stated by Saint Athanasius of Alexandria as thus
"For He, indeed, assumed humanity that we might become God. He manifested Himself by means of a body in order that we might perceive the Mind of the unseen Father. He endured shame from men that we might inherit immortality."
I pray Nico/Lindsay can find this Truth someday and come to inherit the kingdom as I do for you too Chloë. 
I linked in the comment to Ellie's song Keep On Dancing as it premiered on Annie Mac's @R1Dance of @BBCOne. I really enjoyed the song and thought of the cognitive associations I had made to the quotes from Nico/Lindsay as well as a @TaylorSwift13 song Shake It Off, which I like but don't like the music video or one specific lyric that takes the Lord's name in vain.
I related the both Ellie's and Taylor Swift song to my dealing with the affliction I have with hearing voices which has been attributed to my schizophrenia. Just keep on dancing and shake it off, and in the words of Nico/Lindsay never stop dancing ever upward.
The next image is of the surrealist painter Remedios Varo’s creation Creación de las aves, Creation of the birds. At the time I related it to the mythological Athena, Avatar of Wisdom.
I connected it to the mythical creature's attributes of mastery of wisdom, science and techne as well as the intellect. It reminded me of Athene noctua the companion and symbol of Athena representing a sharp intellect as well as the ability to see through darkness.
Varo’s synthesis in the painting shows a creator with supreme intuition along with an absolute command over an inner domain.
I found this painting to be enigmatic and relating to the story I was trying to weave together at the time with the mythological Athena portrayed as an owl. I've since reimagine the work and have distanced it from the pagan mythology I was intrigued by, though I find some of the ideas useful, washed of their idolatry. 
The text of the post states, in relation to what mentioned in a reply earlier about creative practitioners, recognizing is an analytical part of patterning, with forming being the creative act of constructing new patterns.
I had thought of this at the time to be reflective of what I was trying to create with the threads I posted and the Bricolage art I constructed. Such deep layers of meaning espoused as know-brow design meant to not be an exoticism of the weird but rather touch upon a universality inherent within all of human experience that resonates amongst everyone.
I now see this all as being much more than I had planned. Quite an artistic undertaking. I pray the Holy Spirit guided me or at least fixed my errors and erroneous thinking.
May the Immaculata, Mary the Ever Virgin Blessed spouse of the Holy Spirit, Mother of the Word Incarnate, guide you in digesting this Bricolage along with our victorious Divine King and Savior, the Word made flesh, Our Lord Jesus Christ, God and Man.
May his Sacred Heart along with the Immaculate Heart of Mary show you the Way of salvation into Eternal Life.
I didn't plan on writing all this today, but it seems to have come together nicely and is apropos to the entire discourse I have relayed.

Pax Christi Sit Semper Vobiscum

All sixty-six books are Scripture. 

The audience tells you which program you are in. 

Israel, the Jews, the circumcision, and the kingdom are one program. 

The Body of Christ, neither Jew nor Gentile, is the other. Romans through Philemon are the GOSPEL and the INSTRUCTIONS for TODAY.

To Israel, the Jews, the circumcision, and the fathers:

• Genesis: mankind first, then Abraham and his seed, the fathers of Israel.

• Exodus: Israel, the circumcised nation brought out of Egypt and put under the law.

• Leviticus: Israel, the priests and the congregation under the covenant.

• Numbers: Israel in the wilderness.

• Deuteronomy: the next generation of Israel, the circumcision, before the land.

History of Israel:

• Joshua: Israel taking the promised land.

• Judges: Israel before the kings.

• Ruth: Israel, in the line of David. 

• 1 and 2 Samuel: Israel under Samuel, Saul, and David.

• 1 and 2 Kings: Israel and Judah.

• 1 and 2 Chronicles: Judah, the circumcision, after the exile.

• Ezra: the returned remnant of the Jews.

• Nehemiah: the Jews rebuilding Jerusalem. 

• Esther: the Jews in the Persian dispersion.

Wisdom written in Israel’s setting:

• Job: a man outside the covenant, before Israel’s law.

• Psalms: Israel, David, and the temple.

• Proverbs: Israel, and the simple who will hear.

• Ecclesiastes: Israel, the king in Jerusalem.

• Song of Solomon: Israel, the beloved and the king.

Prophets to Israel, Judah, and the nations around them:

• Isaiah: Judah and Jerusalem, and the nations.

• Jeremiah: Judah and Jerusalem.

• Lamentations: Judah in the ruin of Jerusalem.

• Ezekiel: the captives of Judah in Babylon.

• Daniel: Judah in Babylon, and the future of Israel.

• Hosea: the northern kingdom of Israel.

• Joel: Judah and Jerusalem.

• Amos: Israel.

• Obadiah: Edom, concerning Israel.

• Jonah: Nineveh, and Israel through the prophet.

• Micah: Samaria and Jerusalem.

• Nahum: Nineveh.

• Habakkuk: Judah.

• Zephaniah: Judah and Jerusalem.

• Haggai: the returned Jews in Jerusalem.

• Zechariah: the returned Jews in Jerusalem.

• Malachi: the Jews of the remnant.

Kingdom writings to Israel, the circumcision:

• Matthew: the Jews, the King and the kingdom.

• Mark: readers beyond Judea, still the kingdom gospel to Israel.

• Luke: Theophilus, still the earthly ministry to Israel.

• John: Israel, that they might believe Jesus is the Christ.

• Acts: Israel first. The kingdom is offered to the circumcision, then Israel falls and the body of Christ begins. Early Acts is not the pattern for today.

To the body of Christ: our gospel and our instructions for today:

These thirteen are Paul’s epistles. Here there is neither Jew nor Gentile. The middle wall is down. Salvation is by grace through faith in Christ crucified, buried, and risen. THIS IS YOUR MAIL.

• Romans: saints in Rome, Jew and Gentile made one body.

• 1 Corinthians: the church at Corinth, the body of Christ.

• 2 Corinthians: the church at Corinth, the body of Christ.

• Galatians: the churches of Galatia, warned against going back under the circumcision, to the body of Christ.

• Ephesians: the saints and faithful in Christ Jesus, one new man, to the body of Christ.

• Philippians: the saints at Philippi, to the body of Christ.

• Colossians: the saints at Colosse, complete in Christ, to the body of Christ.

• 1 Thessalonians: the church of the Thessalonians, to the body of Christ.

• 2 Thessalonians: the church of the Thessalonians, to the body of Christ.

• 1 Timothy: Timothy, for order in the church which is his body, to the body of Christ.

• 2 Timothy: Timothy, to the body of Christ.

•Titus: Titus, to the body of Christ.

•Philemon: Philemon and the church in his house, to the body of Christ.

To the Hebrews, the twelve tribes, the dispersion, and Israel in the day of the Lord:

Not the body-of-Christ pattern for today. NOT to the body of Christ.

Cont..

THE OPERATIONAL BRIEFING (WEEK OF 05 Oct – 11 Oct 2026)
FOR ZODIACAL ADVENTURING, SPECULATIVE FUN, AND NON-SERIOUS FICTIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.
(Seasonal mobility and local tracking reflect the Southern Axis.)

GENERAL SCOUT (The Ground Terrain)
START OF WEEK: Sun in Libra (Air) / Moon in Cancer (Water) — Steady terrain. Air keeps the line of sight. Water keeps the step close to camp. Check the near edge before a claim leaves the stash.
END OF WEEK: Sun in Libra (Air) / Moon in Libra (Air) — Steady terrain. Both lights share the scales, so the floor does not sink. Pack the hideaway. The Scorpio threshold waits past midnight, outside this week.
SEASONAL MOBILITY BIAS: Spring — Awaken, explore, cultivate
TRIBAL MOBILITY: Monday opens soft under a Cancer Moon, mood close and courtly. Sunday closes lighter on a Libra Moon, mood spare and reset. Movement — Mon Hold, Tue Steady, Wed Hold, Thu Steady, Fri Steady, Sat Steady, Sun Hold.

EARTH CYCLE (Earth Elemental Phase)
EARTH DYNAMIC: Libra Air (23 Sep → 23 Oct) → next: Scorpio (23 Oct). Stage: Early. Air is still setting the terms. The vault has not passed to water. Southern spring asks the outpost to cultivate what is already named.
GROWTH GOVERNOR: Jupiter in Leo (Fire) — Direct. Growth shows as a brighter court, a supply that wants witnesses, a position that expands by being seen. Motion stays outward. The ledger does not turn inward.
JUPITER EFFECT: Jupiter in Leo widens a supply that already has a name, and leaves an unmarked stash small.
TRIBAL SUPPLY: Keep the shown cache and the quiet reserve on different trails. Move only what the brief already holds. Jupiter directly feeds the court, and the thinning light into the 11 Oct gate says stock the waypoint before the dark.

LIGHT CYCLE (Moon Phase)
START PHASE: Waning Crescent (38%) Yang with 62% Yin — Moon in Cancer (Water). Tide still falling, cover close over the camp.
PEAK LUNATION: New Moon on 11 Oct in Libra — the dark gate, once, at 01:50 AEST.
END PHASE: Waxing Crescent (1%) Yang with 99% Yin — Moon in Libra (Air). Tide has only just turned. The road is still a whisper.
TRIBAL VISIBILITY: The Moon runs from a Cancer hold into the Libra dark, and still holds Libra at the close. Ambient tide drops until the New Moon, then barely lifts. Scout by cover, rest the loud claim, and treat Sunday’s dark as the fresh threshold. Last cross into the peak sign is 09 Oct.

COUNSEL ASPECTS (This week’s additional counsel)
Moon Conjunction Mars (05 Oct): Tide and push share one degree. Use the charge inside camp, not on the open road.
Moon Square Venus (05 Oct): Pull and tide cross. Do not broker in the first dark hours.
Moon Conjunction Jupiter (06 Oct): The store lights beside the Moon. Claim a visible supply, then step back.
Mercury Conjunction Venus (07 Oct): Cipher and pull share one Scorpio room. Say the private thing once, then seal it.
Venus Square Mars (11 Oct): Pull and push lock after the gate. The heat is real. The reception is not ready.
TRIBAL COUNSEL: Tone is sealed, not a rally. Trust Monday’s conjunction for a contained charge, Wednesday’s conjunction for what may be said, and Tuesday’s store-light if the claim is already yours. Keep the 05 Oct square off the table. Rest the 11 Oct square, and do not reopen what the New Moon has only just hidden.

TACTICAL RECONNAISSANCE: (This week’s additional reconnaissance)
Mercury START Scorpio Water / Mercury END Scorpio Water — it sat there all week.
MOTION: Direct
VOICE: Decode
HITS: Moon Square Mercury (05 Oct)
TRIBAL RECONNAISSANCE: Mercury holds the water outpost and stays direct, so the map is readable if the tribe decodes rather than broadcasts. The 05 Oct square is noise on the line. The 07 Oct meeting with Venus is the window to name the secret and file it. No ingress, no station. Navigate by trace, not by rumor.

AETHERIAL FIELD (Spirit & Consciousness)
THE ALCHEMY OF EMOTION: A private pull runs under a public scale. It wants the hideaway and the fair court at once. Sunday’s square is the snag, not the verdict.
THE MAGICAL ENERGY CURRENT: Voltage thins toward the Libra dark and spikes only at 01:50 AEST on 11 Oct. Wednesday carries a short side-current. After the gate, do not draw on what is left.
FIELD CLASS DYNAMIC: Rogue with Virgo (Earth). Close range, hidden, work kept inside the coat. Take the near trail, not the ridge. Cover is the tactic. A loud claim wastes the week. Quiet after the errand is part of the approach.
Start: crescent still falling, Cancer water at the heel — first steps stay inside camp.
Hinge: New Moon 11 Oct, Libra dark — the only true gate. Seal one pact, then go quiet.
End: a hair of new light, still Libra — recover the tool, do not test it.

REAR WATCH: (Planetary Retrogrades)
Retrograde — Venus in Scorpio (Water) — already retrograde; ends 14 Nov; old receptions return before new ones land.
Retrograde — Neptune in Aries (Fire) — retrograde; ends 13 Dec; the far signal blurs a first push. Do not trust a vision with no trail.
Retrograde — Pluto in Aquarius (Air) — retrograde; ends 16 Oct; the deep code is still in revision. A public rewrite can wait.
Retrograde — Saturn in Aries (Fire) — retrograde; ends 10 Dec; the limit sits on the ignition. Check the charge before it runs.
Retrograde — Uranus in Gemini (Air) — retrograde; ends 08 Feb 2027; the side-road flickers. Take the short passage. Do not chase every whisper.
Direct — Mars in Leo (Fire) — direct; next Rx 10 Jan 2027; the push still runs forward in the fire sign.
Direct — Jupiter in Leo (Fire) — direct; next Rx 13 Dec; growth still faces outward, wider than the week can spend.
Direct — Mercury in Scorpio (Water) — direct; next Rx 24 Oct; the voice can still decode. The reversal is not this week.
REAR WATCH DYNAMIC: No station falls inside 05–11 Oct. Venus is already walking backward from 03 Oct, so review the bond before Monday’s camp opens. Use 07 Oct for the one Mercury–Venus seal. Leave 11 Oct unforced: the square meets a retrograde Venus, and the heat will not take a clean reception. Pluto’s direct turn is 16 Oct, outside this span.

VENUS REPORT (The Pull)
START OF WEEK: Venus in Scorpio (Water) - Retrograde. The pull is already retracing a private sign.
END OF WEEK: Venus in Scorpio (Water) - Retrograde. Same water, same reverse, closer to the square.
DAILY MULTIPLIERS START OF WEEK ALLOCATION:
Yin Hunter: 13% — A small private probe, only if the brief is already sealed.
Yin Gatherer: 67% — The main line: recover the old reception, stash what is not ready for court.
Yang Hunter: 7% — Almost no open charge. Do not stage the pull.
Yang Gatherer: 13% — A thin outer reserve, enough for a fair face and nothing more.
ALLOCATION MODE: GATHERER

text:
Fastest economy, weakest market

by Prabhu Chawla 

Behind these abstractions stand real people. The stock market clerk in Kanpur and the nurse in Kochi who poured a few thousand rupees each month into an SIP were promised that patience pays

Ninety years ago, John Maynard Keynes compared the stock market to a newspaper beauty contest. Readers win not by choosing the prettiest face, but by guessing which face everyone else will choose. In The General Theory he formulated the game's ultimate refinement: “We have reached the third degree where we devote our intelligences to anticipating what average opinion expects the average opinion to be.” Keynes fathomed that prices are verdicts on belief, not inventories of fact. India has spent the past eight weeks relearning his lesson at a ruinous price.

Even a cursory glance at the facts ought to have flattered India. Its economy grew by 7.8 percent between April and June, much faster than every major rival. Its fifty biggest listed companies swelled their profits by 18 percent, the steepest climb in ten quarters. Yet on last Friday, the Sensex closed at 71,910, bruised by its eighth losing week in a row. It was its longest streak of falls since the Covid 2020. The jury of Keynes's contest had studied India's handsome figures and they chose another face.

Both the financial and political costs of the Indian market mayhem were staggering. Since August 5, the index has lost nearly 6,700 points, about 8.5 percent. On a rough reckoning, between ₹30 lakh crore and ₹40 lakh crore of market capitalisations has evaporated. Measured against other emerging markets, India has turned in its weakest performance in more than two decades.

Behind these abstractions stand real people. The stock market clerk in Kanpur and the nurse in Kochi who poured a few thousand rupees each month into an SIP were promised that patience pays. They did not lose their savings in a single terrifying afternoon. They watched them seep away week after weary week. The humiliation lies in the company India kept. In the same weeks the Nasdaq struck a record, Korea's Kospi reclaimed 7,000 and Japan's Nikkei loitered near its summit. Across 2026, Seoul has soared about 68 percent, Tokyo by 29 percent and New York by 13 percent. The Sensex has sunk more than 12 percent in rupees and nearly 18 percent in dollars. All weathered the same war, the same crude and the same Fed. They flourished while India floundered.

The plunge unfolded in three acts. In August, oil crept upward as Washington and Tehran squared up across the Strait of Hormuz. In September, the Federal Reserve raised rates, American bond yields reached their highest since 2007 and the rupee crashed through 96 to the dollar. Then, on September 28, US President Donald Trump spurned Iran's peace proposal. That day 47 of the 50 Nifty stocks fell, in a session that was less a retreat than a rout.

Why did India alone bleed? The storm was shared, but the ships were not. Three haemorrhages, long patched and long postponed, burst open together. The first was oil. India imported most of the crude it burnt, so every price surge swelled the import bill, sank the rupee and stoked inflation, which reached 4.82 percent in August. Carmakers, ports and engineering firms, all wagers on India's own growth, headed the casualty list. The second haemorrhage was artificial intelligence, the gold rush of this decade. Korea's chip exports leaped about 170 percent in eight months as Samsung and SK hynix sold the memory that data centres devour. India sells the world almost none of that hardware, and its proud IT giants are cast as prey for automation rather than its predators. When global capital went shopping for the future, they found India's shelves empty. How, then, can booming profits coexist with a bleeding market? Benjamin Graham, the mentor of Warren Buffett, supplied the answer long ago. In the short run, he taught, the market is a voting machine; in the long run, it is a weighing machine. GDP weighs the quarter just gone. Share prices are votes on the year ahead, cast by people who can move their money to Seoul before lunch. Those voters saw softer consumption and an oil shock with no end in sight. Even the Reserve Bank of India expected growth to cool to 6.4 to 6.8 percent. When External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar warned the United Nations last month of a crisis in fuel, food, fertiliser and finance, he gave voice to fears the market had already priced.

What happens next hinges partly on forces far from New Delhi? When the Reserve Bank meets on October 7, it must choose between shielding the rupee and sparing borrowers. A ceasefire in the Gulf would revive Indian shares faster than any budget. Yet hope is not a policy. India is now cheaper against its peers than at any point in two decades. The real question is whether India can give investors a reason to return.

It can, if it builds on three pillars at once. The Modi government must deliver a liberal dose of vitamin M (more money) for boosting domestic demand. Indian savers have already shown their steel. During the last week of September, foreigners sold about ₹11,500 crore of shares, while domestic institutions bought ₹16,400 crore. A market anchored in a confident consumer is far less hostage to a fund manager in London or New York. The second accelerator is investment. Fixed investment grew by almost 12 percent in the June quarter, and it must now be aimed squarely at the wounds this September exposed. Every rupee spent on solar power, storage and electric transport trims the war tax India pays whenever crude spikes. Every serious wager on chips, electronics and data centres offers global capital something it cannot yet buy in Mumbai.

The third booster is trust, and it is the hardest to build. Capital flees from caprice, as the sudden rise in the tax on derivatives trading showed on Budget day in February. Steady taxes would shrink the premium investors’ demand. So would swifter trade deals with America, Europe and the Gulf, and a diplomacy that secures energy rather than bemoaning its price. India has long told the world it is the next great market. Now it must behave like one. None of this will restore the lost lakhs of crores by Diwali. Yet the lesson is plain. India's economy did not fail these past eight weeks; investors' faith did. Keynes's conviction rewards the face the crowd expects to win. India must now make itself that face.

text:
In “White Gold” author Giles Milton gives a vivid account of the white slave trade, based on letters and manuscripts that survived from the time, several written by slaves. In one account Milton describes how in July 1625 a fleet of over twenty ships manned with Barbary pirates arrived in the thick sea mist and headed up the coast of Cornwall. Many coastal communities were completely destroyed. In 1625 the mayor of Plymouth estimated that the pirates destroyed 1000 fishing boats and a similar number of villagers were carried off into slavery in one summer alone.

Amongst the most notorious slave markets at the time was the souk in the walled city of Sale in Morocco. Milton visited Sale, walking the same path “trodden by wretched European slaves – men, women and children whose steps were slowed by the weight of their iron chains and shackles”. Once sold, most disappeared without trace, subjected to a living hell, as described by slave Robert Adams who was captured in 1620. 

The manuscript of a Cornish boy from Penryn named Thomas Pellow who was captured at sea in 1715 at the age of 11, which Milton quotes in his book, offers valuable insight into the persecution of the white slaves. He became a personal slave to the Sultan of Morocco, Moulay Ismail, in the imperial capital of Meknes. Despite being subjected to a botched circumcision operation after he was forced to convert to Islam (known as ‘turning Moor’) and thrashed senseless on many occasion, he survived to tell his tale. In 1737 at the age of 33, after 23 years in captivity Pellow managed a successful escape.

He explained that one of the Sultan’s many perverted pastimes was to marry off his slaves. He was particularly fond of mulattos or mixed race slaves and started his own “breeding programme”, matching white male slaves with black North African women while white women slaves were incarcerated in his harem and forced to breed. He would line up his slaves and citizens and call out “that one, take that one”.

The white slave trade continued well into the 1800s when the United States of America, Britain and several European nations finally came together and fought and won two wars against the Barbary pirates.

The Barbary empires went into decline from then onwards but the white slave trade continued, albeit to a lesser extent, even after France took control of Algeria and Tunisia in 1830 and 1831, and Britain passed the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. At the same time European governments passed laws granting emancipation to slaves.

As Europe’s power increased it gradually diminished the power of the sultans, North African merchants and slave traders. Italy ultimately took control of Libya (Tripoli) in 1911 and one year later Morocco became a protectorate of France.

The people in the coastal villages of Britain and Europe could finally live in relative peace, but not for long. Within a few years another demon had raised it’s  head that led to another era of mass slaughter and brutality, human against human. We called this World War I.
